steps.title: Prepare GelBond® slides
steps.instruction: Cut GelBond® sheets (Lonza, Switzerland) into 25 × 55 mm strips. Apply a small amount of Norland Optical Adhesive 68 (Thorlabs Inc., US‑NJ) to the edge of the frosted side of a 26 × 76 mm microscope slide. Place the GelBond® strip on the slide with the hydrophobic side down (water beads up), press lightly to bond, and UV‑irradiate at 365 nm for 20 s. Repeat for all slides, assign a random identifier to each, and store the prepared slides dry in a dust‑free environment.

substeps.instruction: Apply Norland Optical Adhesive 68 to frosted edge of 26 × 76 mm slide.
Place strip hydrophobic side down on slide.
Repeat for all slides and label.

steps.title: Pre‑heat equipment and reagents
steps.instruction: Set water bath and heating plate to 37 °C and begin warming cell growth medium. Prepare lysis and electrophoresis working solutions and keep them on ice (4 °C). Melt one aliquot of PBS‑agarose in a microwave at 300 W for ~1 min, then place the molten agarose in the 37 °C water bath with the lid closed to avoid condensation. Pre‑cool enough cuvettes (and the horizontal electrophoresis chamber) to 4 °C.

substeps.instruction: Pre‑heat water bath and heat plate to 37 °C.
Prepare lysis and electrophoresis solutions; keep at 4 °C.
Microwave PBS‑agarose at 300 W for ~1 min.
Transfer molten agarose to 37 °C water bath (lid closed).
Pre‑cool cuvettes and electrophoresis chamber to 4 °C.

steps.title: Embed cells in agarose on slides
steps.instruction: Expose cells to the desired xenobiotic in growth medium, mix the cells with low‑melting‑point agarose, and pipette the mixture onto the prepared GelBond®/slide (or GelBond® film). Allow the agarose to solidify, forming a cell‑containing gel layer.

steps.title: Lyse embedded cells
steps.instruction: Submerge the agarose‑embedded slides in cold lysis solution (detergents, high‑salt, pH 8.5) kept at 4 °C, then rinse briefly in a wash solution also adjusted to pH 8.5, to disrupt membranes and proteins and generate protein‑depleted nucleoids.

steps.title: Alkali unwind DNA
steps.instruction: Transfer the slides to the electrophoresis (alkali‑unwinding) solution containing 30 mM LiOH, pH 12.5 (low‑conductivity) and incubate for 2.5 min to relax super‑coiled DNA and release loops and fragments.

steps.title: Run electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Place the slides in the horizontal electrophoresis chamber and apply a voltage six‑times higher than that used in conventional comet assays for 1 min, allowing fragmented DNA to migrate toward the anode.

steps.title: Stain comets
steps.instruction: Rehydrate slides in 0.4 M Tris‑HCl, pH 7.5 for 15 s. Add 20 µl of SYBR® Gold (1:10,000 dilution in 0.4 M Tris‑HCl) and incubate 10 min in a humidity chamber protected from UV light. Wash slides twice for 1 min each in 0.4 M Tris‑HCl, dab off excess liquid, cover the gel with a 24 × 55 mm cover slip, and keep the slides in the humidity chamber to prevent drying.

substeps.instruction: Rehydrate in 0.4 M Tris‑HCl, pH 7.5 for 15 s.
Add 20 µl SYBR® Gold (1:10,000) and incubate 10 min in humidity chamber.
Dab off excess liquid, cover with 24 × 55 mm cover slip.

steps.title: Image and quantify DNA damage
steps.instruction: Capture fluorescence images of the comets using a microscope and analyze them with Comet assay IV software (Perspective Instruments, UK) to obtain parameters such as percentage of DNA in the tail (% TDNA).
